title.value: “Your child needs surgery”: A survey-based evaluation of simulated expert consent conversations by key stakeholders
title.justification: The title of the paper is explicitly stated at the beginning of the document.
title.quote: “Your child needs surgery”: A survey-based evaluation of simulated expert consent conversations by key stakeholders

extractions.description: This study explores the practices of informed consent in pediatric surgeries through a survey-based evaluation. It examines recordings of consent conversations between pediatric surgeons and standardized patients in both low and high-risk surgery scenarios, and gathers feedback from various stakeholders including families and healthcare professionals. The paper identifies strengths and gaps in the current consent process and suggests areas for improvements to facilitate better communication and patient engagement.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper does not discuss climate change or related topics. Its focus is on informed consent conversations in pediatric surgery, without any mention of environmental or climate-related impacts.
climate_change_is_central.quote: Background: Consent conversations in pediatric surgery are essential components of pre-operative care which, when inadequate, can lead to significant adverse consequences for the child, parents, surgeon, and others in the healthcare system.

secondary_categories.quote: A recent systematic review has identified specific interventions for improving patient comprehension, but beyond that relatively little is known about the critical components and their utility in the informed consent process.
